dedupe_keys.name: fews net data explorer and data warehouse api

description: The FEWS NET Data Explorer and its Data Warehouse API hold the data that the Famine Early Warning Systems Network uses for food security early warning: market prices and trade, acute food insecurity classifications and projections compatible with the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), agroclimatology, livelihood zones, crop production, nutrition and geographic boundaries. USAID established FEWS NET in 1985 after famines in East and West Africa; it forecasts acute food insecurity six to twelve months ahead to guide humanitarian planning and response. Coverage is the several dozen most food-insecure countries it monitors in East, Southern and West Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Europe, and Latin America and the Caribbean, at country, livelihood-zone, administrative-unit and market level, with series such as monthly prices. Access: the Data Explorer lets users search, filter, visualise and export data, and the Data Warehouse REST API at fdw.fews.net/api returns public data without authentication and more with an account. Cost is free; the data usage policy is set per source document, and some data are restricted. Caveats: the Data Explorer does not expose all FEWS NET data, series lengths differ by country and source, and continuity depends on funding. Simulation uses: food supply and market disruption scenarios, drought and climate impacts on food systems, and emergency response planning for food assistance. Related: IPC analyses and WFP DataBridges food prices are listed in the register but not yet catalogued.
